correctness.rationale: For k<r, Y=k iff the untrimmed Poisson total equals k; at k=r all extra configurations comprise j>r singleton observations, with exact mass e^{-mλ} binom(m,j)λ^j. This proves the strictly negative ULC determinant. A positive increasing polynomial yields the unique ordinary-LC local threshold, and positive falling-factorial coefficients give monotone rescaled thresholds converging by dominated convergence. The max endpoint invokes the published order-statistic preservation theorem. Independently enumerated factorial-weight polynomial coefficients pass 346 finite exact comparisons.

value.rationale: The upper trimmed total is a natural count-data summary bridging maximum and full sum. The result gives a complete sharp preservation boundary for every sample size and intensity, tied to the first low-tail mass that departs from Poisson. The unique ordinary-log-concavity crossover and its decreasing rescaled asymptotic root give a meaningful parameterized structural description, not a one-off counterexample.
